title: When the Inheritance Wakes Revisited
premise: When a confession letter postmarked the day after Edith Amberdale's funeral arrives at estate lawyer Jonah Amberdale's office, he discovers the will he read five years ago was forged—and the real one names a beneficiary who officially never existed. As Jonah follows the letter's cryptic instructions, he realizes the killer is someone with privileged access to the town's sealed case files, someone who has been watching him alphabetize their secrets for years. His investigation collides with his growing love for Mara Quill, the coroner's clerk whose testimony could either convict the killer or destroy her own family. In the end, Jonah chooses justice outside the law: he lets the killer believe they've won, then springs a trap at the reading of the true will, where a recorded confession and the beneficiary herself—Edith's hidden daughter—confront the murderer before the town.
about_author: Emrys Vane is the pen name of a former small-town probate clerk who spent a decade watching families fracture over inheritance papers. Vane writes mysteries about the quiet violence hidden in legal documents and the towns that keep them sealed.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Three days after Edith Amberdale's funeral, Jonah receives a confession letter describing a murder no one has reported—dated five years ago, the night of the will reading he presided over. The letter names him as its only intended reader. Rattled, he cross-checks the estate file and finds the will's signature page subtly altered. Emotional beat: dread blooming in a man who trusted paper more than people.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, shifting to Mara's midway. Jonah quietly reopens the old case, drawing the attention of Mara Quill, who warns him the coroner's report was doctored by her late father. Their uneasy alliance deepens as they map who had access to the sealed files—and realize the suspect pool includes the town's most beloved figures. Emotional beat: two lonely archivists discovering that love is a liability they can't file away.

chapters.title: What the Dead Sign Twice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The killer strikes: Mara is attacked, the original will stolen, and Jonah receives a second letter proving his adversary has read his private case notes. Realizing the beneficiary—Edith's secret daughter, Lark—will be next, Jonah locates her hiding in a neighboring county. He decides to stage a public reading of the true will, betting the killer cannot resist appearing. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into cold, deliberate resolve.

chapters.title: Read Aloud, Witnessed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV with Lark's testimony interwoven. At the staged reading, Jonah reads the true will aloud while a hidden recorder captures the killer's confession, provoked by a forged letter he planted in the old files. Sheriff's deputies—warned off the record—take the killer, Edith's trusted executor, into custody. Jonah and Mara, both compromised by what they did outside the law, choose each other anyway. Emotional beat: justice delivered off the books, love chosen over duty.
